Alex / team,

Attached are the materials requested: an updated network diagram (redwood_network_diagram_v2.png), an isolation matrix CSV, and a short threat model summary (PDF). Highlights below — please see attachments for diagrams and the isolation matrix.

Attachment stubs:
- redwood_network_diagram_v2.png (png, 920KB) - detailed diagram showing Hosted API (multi-tenant) and Private (VPC peered / on-prem) topologies.
- redwood_isolation_matrix.csv (csv, 45KB) - per-component isolation, encryption, and tenancy characteristics.
- redwood_threat_model_summary.pdf (pdf, 48KB) - 2-page summary (data-plane/control-plane/supply-chain).

Summary (concise):
1) Deployment isolation
   - Hosted API: logical tenant isolation at application and model-serving layer. Each customer has dedicated runtime namespaces with per-tenant KV cache segmentation. Network: traffic originates from Redwood-managed VPCs. Customer data at rest is encrypted with per-tenant keys (CMK).
   - Private (VPC) deployment: customer gets a private control plane connection via PrivateLink or VPC peering depending on cloud provider. Data plane can be configured to only traverse customer VPC. On-prem option supports air-gapped installs.

2) Control plane vs Data plane separation
   - Control plane (orchestration, billing/telemetry) is logically separated and can be configured to be customer-accessible or entirely customer-managed in Private deployments. TLS 1.3 + mTLS for control plane APIs.

3) Key management (KMS/HSM)
   - BYOK: supported. Customers can bring keys to Redwood-managed HSM or use customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with envelope encryption. We support HSM-backed keys for highest assurance.

4) Network connectivity and port/IP requirements (high level)
   - For PrivateLink/VPC peering: outbound connections to control-plane endpoints on TCP 443.
   - For on-prem installs: we provide a minimal list of egress IP ranges and port requirements (will share in a follow-up CSV).

5) Threat model highlights (see PDF)
   - Data exfiltration: mitigations include per-tenant encryption, strict egress filtering, and KV cache auto-ttl.
   - Model poisoning: model artifacts are versioned and hashed; model onboarding requires signed artifacts and provenance checks.
   - Supply chain: build pipelines are signed and reproducible; third-party dependencies scanned with SCA tools.

6) Compliance artifacts
   - SOC 2 Type II report and recent network pen-test summary are available under NDA. We can share redacted copies through your secure intake link.

Please let us know if you want the detailed egress IP list or a recorded walk-through of the diagram.

Thanks,

Alex — quick answers below, and attached is a minimal firewall/egress CSV we maintain for customers. We'll also upload the pen-test exec summary to your secure intake.

1) Shared Hosted pools and cross-tenant protections:
   - We do run multi-tenant serving pools for the Hosted API, but model weights are isolated per-tenant at the runtime level. We do not execute arbitrary untrusted code in the same address space as customer models. Mitigations: process-level isolation, JIT hardening where applicable, cache-key segregation, and scheduled noise injection for timing-obfuscation in high-sensitivity deployments. We also offer dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) for customers requiring physical isolation.

2) Air-gapped / on-prem installs:
   - Yes, Redwood supports an air-gapped on-prem installation. Features restricted in air-gapped mode: automatic model catalog updates (manual import required), certain telemetry/observability shippers (local collection only), and remote rollback orchestration. Control plane can be run locally per customer. KMS must be customer-provided in fully air-gapped installs.

3) Egress/ports (summary):
   - Control plane endpoints: TCP 443 (HTTPS) outbound to redwood-control.redwood.example.com (can be replaced with customer-provided endpoints in Private deployments).
   - Model pull / artifact fetch: TCP 443 outbound to artifact-store.redwood.example.com (or via offline artifact import for air-gapped installs).
   - Optional telemetry: outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood.example.com (can be disabled).

   Full CSV attached: [attachment: redwood_egress_ranges.csv (csv, 4KB)]

4) Pen test / compliance artifacts:
   - We'll share the redacted SOC2 Type II and the pen-test executive summary through your intake link. Please confirm the intake URL and we will upload within 24 hours.

Summary of mitigations in the threat model PDF (already attached):
   - Least privilege and segmented roles for control plane ops
   - Cryptographic separation (per-tenant CMKs, envelope encryption)
   - Image signing and SBOMs for build artifacts
   - Runtime attestation for Private deployments (optional)

If useful, we can schedule a 30-min technical readout with Dev and Hiro to walk through the diagram and port table.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
